system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

exchanges.user:
ISSUES:
- SPA-N-001 | General liability cap | seller's draft: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 general cap
- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
The Seller’s assertions of “market standard”, principal-level agreement and “FINAL” status are not evidence of Buyer approval. The positions below are **Buyer negotiating recommendations**, subject to the complete SPA and underlying diligence documents.

| Issue | Seller’s position | What Buyer should want | Recommendation — one-line reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001 General liability cap** | General warranty liability capped at **20% / AUD 4.8m**. | Meaningful recovery proportionate to risk, with separate protection for fundamental, tax and identified risks. | **Counter at 50% / AUD 12m**, subject to diligence and recovery security; keep special categories outside this cap — 20% leaves substantial acquisition risk with Buyer. |
| **SPA-N-002 De minimis & basket** | Claims must exceed **AUD 25,000**; **AUD 250,000 deductible basket**, recovering only excess. | Lower thresholds, related-claim aggregation and a tipping basket; no thresholds for special categories. | **Propose AUD 10,000 de minimis and AUD 120,000 tipping basket**, aggregating related claims — the proposed combination can eliminate meaningful recovery for repeated smaller breaches. |
| **SPA-N-003 General claims time limit** | Notice within **18 months**; limitations presumptively apply to all Claims. | At least two full reporting cycles to identify general breaches; distinct periods for other categories. | **Seek 24 months for general warranties**, with timely notified claims surviving until resolved — 18 months may expire before latent issues emerge. |
| **SPA-N-004 Fundamental/Title regime** | Capacity and title subject to general cap and time limits. | Separate warranties covering authority, ownership, fully paid shares, no encumbrances and all issued equity; materially longer protection. | **Seek a 100% price cap and seven-year contractual notification period**, subject to applicable law, without basket/de minimis — ownership and authority are core consideration risks, not ordinary business risks. |
| **SPA-N-005 Fraud carve-out** | Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to all Claims; no express fraud exception supplied. | Express preservation of fraud claims and remedies, including relevant fraudulent conduct by Seller representatives. | **Exclude fraud and fraudulent concealment/misrepresentation from caps, thresholds, deadlines, disclosure/knowledge bars, exclusive remedy and non-reliance**, preserving non-excludable rights — Seller must not obtain contractual protection for fraud. |
| **SPA-N-006 Disclosure scope** | Blanket disclosure of the data room, accounts, registers and public records. | Only sufficiently detailed, fair disclosure against identifiable warranties; fixed, accessible disclosure record. | **Reject blanket deemed disclosure; require specific, intelligible disclosures and an archived data-room index**, with no qualification of specific indemnities unless expressly agreed — document availability does not establish informed acceptance of a risk. |
| **SPA-N-007 Buyer knowledge qualifier** | No claim for matters Buyer or advisers knew, including anything discoverable from records. | No constructive/imputed knowledge bar; preferably no Buyer-knowledge exclusion. | **Delete; fallback limited to actual conscious knowledge of named Buyer individuals of the specific breach at signing**, excluding adviser imputation and inquiry duties — discoverability otherwise transfers diligence risk wholesale to Buyer. |
| **SPA-N-008 Bluefen consent** | Reasonable endeavours; condition satisfied by delivery of written consent, described as “addressed”. | Effective change-control consent satisfying clause 11.3 conditions, without unacceptable commercial concessions. | **Make satisfactory consent and fulfilment of associated conditions a Buyer-waivable completion condition**, with evidence and a long-stop right — approximately 30% of revenue is exposed and no final consent is supplied. |
| **SPA-N-009 Riverlark facility** | Approximately **AUD 3.2m** outstanding; security release after Completion. | Debt repayment and effective security/guarantee releases at Completion, consistent with debt-free/cash-free pricing. | **Require lender payout figures, direct payment through funds flow and binding simultaneous release arrangements**, with prompt registration clean-up — Buyer should not pay debt-free value while inheriting secured debt or release risk. |
| **SPA-N-010 Employee bonuses** | **AUD 420,000** conditional bonuses are Seller’s matter but omitted from funds flow; on-costs unspecified. | Seller bears transaction-triggered bonuses and applicable payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs, without double counting. | **Quantify and expressly allocate these amounts to Seller through price mechanics/funds flow, backed by an indemnity for residual exposure** — omission can leave the acquired company funding Seller’s transaction costs. |
| **SPA-N-011 Ironquay IP indemnity** | Indemnity limited to the specific SOW3 payment; considers it adequate. | Verified payment and effective ownership of all relevant SOW3 materials, plus protection against resulting title/use disputes. | **Require payment evidence and confirmatory assignment by Completion; broaden the indemnity to resulting ownership, infringement, remediation and enforcement losses** — AUD 180,000 recorded open is not proof of non-payment, but transfer remains unverified. |
| **SPA-N-012 Export/privacy incident** | Preliminary operational matter, not expected to be material; no confirmed breach or quantified loss. | Prompt evidence-based investigation, containment, lawful notification assessment and protection for pre-Completion exposure. | **Require investigation updates, preservation/containment and a specific indemnity for incident-related liabilities and reasonable response costs, supported by retention if warranted** — unresolved access and scope justify protection, not an unsupported finding of a notifiable breach. |
| **SPA-N-013 Sandbar renewals** | Three **AUD 110,000** renewals are ordinary-course costs. | Assess the **AUD 330,000 aggregate** by timing, scope, cancellation rights, accrual and commercial necessity. | **Review together; restrict new commitments pending Completion and allocate only substantiated Seller-period, exceptional or debt-like amounts to Seller** — neither ordinary-course treatment nor a price deduction is established by the disclosure. |
| **SPA-N-014 Category separation** | General limitations and remedies apply to all Claims unless expressly excluded. | Clear, distinct regimes for general warranties, fundamental warranties, tax, specific indemnities, payment/completion obligations and fraud. | **Insert an express category matrix and precedence clause, disapplying general limitations unless specifically adopted** — an “all Claims” provision could silently defeat negotiated special protections. |
| **SPA-N-015 Title verification** | Relies on DD-012 share register showing Seller holds 100%. | Independent verification of issued capital, ownership, encumbrances, options/convertibles and valid transfer mechanics. | **Reconcile registers with corporate records, certificates and issue/transfer history; check security interests and obtain title warranties and completion deliverables** — the register is important evidence, not complete verification of unencumbered ownership. |
| **SPA-N-016 Tax/IP open terms** | Tax and IP treated as settled under the general regime. | Separate pre-Completion tax indemnity and tailored tax warranties; robust IP ownership, licensing and infringement warranties, distinct from Ironquay protection. | **Reopen expressly: tax protection through applicable assessment/reassessment periods plus a claims buffer; negotiate enhanced IP cap/duration after diligence** — tax timing and SaaS IP dependency are not adequately addressed by an undifferentiated general regime. |

**Completion priorities:** Bluefen consent, Riverlark discharge arrangements, bonus allocation, Ironquay ownership evidence and title verification. Disclosure alone should not discharge any of these requirements.
=== END ADVICE ===
